docs.title: rig
docs.text:
rig is a small command-line tool for the mechanical parts of a branch-per-task workflow: pushing a task branch, opening and reading pull requests, waiting for CI, keeping tasks, findings and notes, and printing where the work stands. It was built for claude-kit, where coding agents run these steps many times a day, but it does not depend on the kit.

It exists for two reasons:

  • A narrow push. rig push takes a task id or a branch name and nothing else. It cannot push the default branch, a tag, a refspec or a force push, so it is safe to allow without a prompt.
  • One interface over two forges. The same commands and the same output work on GitHub and GitLab. rig runs gh or glab underneath and uses the login you already have. It stores a token only for Jira, which has no such tool, and then in the OS keychain.
  • Tasks and rules you define. Tasks, findings and notes live in your repository's git directory, outside any branch. A workflow file you write says which states a task passes through and what must be true before each move, and rig refuses a move that breaks it. See docs/workflows.md.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
rig needs Go 1.24 or later, git, and gh (GitHub) or glab (GitLab).

go install github.com/AindriuB/rig/cmd/rig@v0.3.0

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
rig push <task-id|branch> [--worktree <path>]
rig pr view [<pr|branch> | --task <id>] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig pr list [--mine] [--head <branch>] [--state open|closed|merged] [--limit <n>] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig pr checks [<pr|branch> | --task <id>] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig pr open --head <branch> --title <text> [--base <branch>] [--body <text>] [--draft] [--repo <dir>]
rig pr wait <pr-number | --run <run-id>> [--repo <dir>]
rig status [--json]
rig task new --slug <s> --title <text> [--body <text> | --body-file <path>] [--field <name>=<value>]... [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig task show <task> [--findings] [--notes] [--history] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig task edit <task> [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig task list [--state <s>]... [--all] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig task move <task> <state> [--sha <sha>] [--pr <n>] [--reason <text>] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig task set <task> --field <name>=<value>... [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig task count <task> <counter> [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig task is <task> <state> [--repo <dir>]
rig task log <task> [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig finding add <task> --severity <sev> --summary <text> [--path <p[:line]>] [--key <k>] [--field <name>=<value>]... [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig finding list <task> [--status <s>]... [--blocking] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig finding set <task> <finding> --status <s> [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig note add [<task>] --kind <k> --text <text> [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig note list [<task>] [--kind <k>] [--limit <n>] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig workflow show [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig workflow validate [<file>] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig next [--who agent|human] [--limit <n>] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig context <task> [--budget <tokens>] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig config get <key> [--global|--repo|--local] [--json]
rig config set <key> <value> --global|--repo|--local
rig config unset <key> --global|--repo|--local
rig config list [--global|--repo|--local] [--show-origin] [--json]
rig login
rig login <service> [--url <site>] [--user <email>] [--repo] [--store keychain|file]
rig login status [--json]
rig logout <service> [--url <site>] [--repo]
rig version
Command What it does Exit codes rig push Pushes one branch to origin. A task id such as 07 resolves to task/07-<slug>. 0 pushed; 1 the push failed; 2 refused, git never ran rig pr view, checks, list Prints pull requests and their CI state in one neutral form. 0; 2 on any error rig pr open Opens a pull request for a branch that is already pushed. It never pushes. 0; 2 on any error rig pr wait Blocks until a pull request's checks, or one CI run, finish. 0 green; 1 red; 2 error or timeout rig status Prints the handoff note, task files, worktrees and open pull requests. 0; 2 on a usage error rig task, rig finding, rig note Create and read tasks, findings and notes, and move a task between states. rig task is answers "is it in this state?" with its exit code. 0; 1 refused by a workflow gate, nothing written; 2 on any error rig workflow Shows the workflow in effect, or checks a workflow file. 0; validate 1 invalid; 2 on any error rig next, rig context List what each open task needs, and print a size-limited brief for one task. They never call the forge. 0; 2 on any error rig config Reads and writes settings in ~/.rig/config.json (--global, --repo) or <repo>/.rig/config.json (--local). rig config set needs a scope. 0; get 1 not set; 2 on any error rig login, rig logout login hands over to gh or glab for GitHub and GitLab, and stores a Jira token in the keychain. rig login status shows where you are logged in, never a token. 0; 1 a login failed; 2 on any error

An unknown flag always exits 2. --json output and the exit codes are a stable contract, described in docs/design.md. The store and the task commands are described in docs/phase-2.md, config and login in docs/phase-2.5.md, and the workflow file format, with a worked example, in docs/workflows.md.

Tasks live in refs/rig/ and .git/rig/ of the clone, so they stay on your machine: rig does not push or fetch them, and a repository looks the same to anyone who does not use rig. With no setup, rig uses a small built-in basic workflow (open, active, done).

docs.title: What rig push will push
docs.text:
A branch is pushed only if all of these hold:

  • it is <prefix>/<name>, and the prefix is in pushPrefixes (by default task and record);
  • it uses only letters, digits and . _ / -;
  • it is not the repository's default branch;
  • it exists locally.

It is pushed to the branch of the same name on origin. There is no option for another remote, a force push or tags.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
rig config holds the newer settings (the forge, the tracker, the workflow); see docs/phase-2.5.md. .claude/rig.json in the repository is optional and still read. Every key has a default.

Key Meaning Default forge github or gitlab detected from the origin host host the forge's host, for a self-hosted instance the origin host pushPrefixes branch prefixes rig push may push ["task", "record"]

pushPrefixes widens what rig push can do without a prompt, so treat the file as yours: do not let an agent edit it unasked.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
go vet ./...

go test ./...

The tests use throwaway git repositories and stub gh and glab programs, so they need no network and no login. The code is in three layers: commands in cmd/rig, the forge interface in internal/forge, and one adapter per forge below it. docs/design.md has the full design and the phases planned next.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
1. Set version in cmd/rig/version.go. A new command, flag or JSON field raises the minor version; a change to an existing one raises the major.
  2. Tag the commit v<version> and push the tag.
  3. The release workflow builds the binaries and drafts a GitHub release.

docs.title: rig: generic actions for agentic workflows
docs.text:
Status: phase 1 was released as 0.1.0. Phases 2 and 2.5 ship together as 0.3.0 and are described in phase-2.md and phase-2.5.md; workflows.md documents the workflow file. Later phases are outlines, each planned separately before it is built.

Direction. rig provides generic actions (tasks, findings, notes, workflow transitions, push, pull requests, CI waits, context briefs, config, login) that any loop can use, driven by any harness: Claude Code, other agent CLIs, CI or a person. It has no built-in lifecycle: a workflow file defines states, transitions and the gates that guard them. claude-kit's loop is one such workflow, owned by the kit. The sections below that describe the kit are the history of how rig started.

rig is its own tool. It was built inside claude-kit under cli/ and moved here with its history in phase 1.5. Nothing in it imports from or reads claude-kit; the kit uses it only through the contract below.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
The kit runs a plan → fanout → review → verify → record loop. Today its state and its rules live in prose and shell text:

  • State is markdown the model re-reads. Task state is parsed out of ## Review round N and ## Wave verified — <sha> sections, then confirmed with gh and git on every turn.
  • Rules are enforced by parsing shell. scripts/push-guard.sh decides whether a Bash command is a safe push by matching its text. A regex cannot understand bash: extending the guard to chained commands took four review rounds, each of which found another way to push to main, and was reverted.
  • It is tied to GitHub. gh is called from scripts/ci-wait.sh and from the status, wave, merged and handoff commands.
  • It does not scale past one developer. Sequential task numbers collide, and PLAN.md and HISTORY.md conflict on merge.

rig is a small Go program that owns the mechanical parts: pushing, pull requests, CI waits and status now; tasks, findings and context later. A command that takes typed arguments can refuse a bad push by construction, where a guard has to recognise one in arbitrary shell.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Go, standard library where possible. One static binary, no runtime.
  • Forge adapters only. gh now, glab next. Git is called directly; there is no git abstraction to swap.
  • The forge is auto-detected from the origin remote's host. .claude/rig.json overrides it.
  • rig holds a token only for a service with no CLI of its own. GitHub and GitLab stay with gh and glab: the adapters shell out to them and use whatever login the user already has, and rig login github|gitlab only hands over to gh auth login or glab auth login. For Jira, which has no such tool, rig login jira stores a token, in the OS keychain unless the user explicitly chooses --store file. No config key holds a token or an account; see phase-2.5.md.
  • No built-in workflow. States, transitions, gates, severities and task fields come from a workflow file; rig ships only a small basic one. What rig enforces whatever the workflow says is listed in phase-2.md.
  • Harness-neutral. The CLI with --json and exit codes, and later an MCP server, are the only surfaces. Nothing assumes Claude Code.
  • scripts/push-guard.sh is unchanged. It stays as the backstop for a raw git push. rig push is the allowed route; the guard is not extended.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Three layers. Only adapters know a technology.

./
  cmd/rig/              commands: policy and output
  internal/forge/       port: Forge interface, PullRequest, Check
  internal/store/       port: Store interface (phase 2)
  internal/forge/github adapter: runs `gh … --json`
  internal/forge/gitlab adapter: runs `glab`
  internal/forge/fake   adapter: in memory, for tests
  internal/git/         rev-parse, push, worktree list, merge-tree
  internal/proc/        shell-free, time-limited subprocess
  internal/config/      .claude/rig.json
  1. Commands (cmd/rig) hold policy and output. Text by default, --json for agents. A command never calls gh, glab or a store backend directly; it calls a port.
  2. Ports (internal/forge, internal/store) are interfaces in neutral types. Nothing in a port names GitHub or GitLab.
  3. Adapters implement a port for one technology. They translate that tool's JSON and vocabulary into the neutral types.

Supporting packages:

  • internal/proc runs a subprocess from an argument vector with a deadline. It never builds a shell string, and it kills the child when the deadline passes.
  • internal/git wraps the handful of git calls rig needs.
  • internal/config reads .claude/rig.json:
Key Meaning Default forge github or gitlab detected from the origin host host forge host, for self-hosted instances the origin host pushPrefixes branch prefixes rig push may push ["task", "record"]

Install with go install github.com/AindriuB/rig/cmd/rig@<tag>. claude-kit's install.sh and install.ps1 install a pinned tag, check rig version against the minimum the kit needs (RIG_MIN_VERSION, declared once in each installer), and carry on with a message when Go or the fetch is missing: the kit's older scripts still work without rig.

docs.title: The contract between rig and its callers
docs.text:
A caller, claude-kit being the first, talks to rig only through its commands, their exit codes and their --json output. It never imports rig's code or reads its files, and rig never reads the kit's. That is what lets rig live in another repository and be versioned on its own.

rig version prints a semantic version (0.1.0 for phase 1, 0.3.0 with phases 2 and 2.5) and exits 0. A new command, flag or JSON field raises the minor version. A change to anything in the tables below raises the major version.

Stable commands and exit codes

Command Exit codes rig version 0 rig push <task-id\|branch> [--worktree <path>] 0 pushed; 1 git ran and the push failed; 2 refused, git push never started rig pr view [<pr\|branch> \| --task <id>] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error, including no such pull request rig pr checks [<pr\|branch> \| --task <id>] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig pr list [--mine] [--head <branch>] [--state open\|closed\|merged] [--limit <n>] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig pr open --head <branch> --title <text> [--base <branch>] [--body <text>] [--draft] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig pr wait <pr-number \| --run <run-id>> [--repo <dir>] 0 green; 1 red; 2 error or timeout rig status [--json] 0; 2 on a usage error rig task new --slug <s> --title <text> [--body <text> \| --body-file <path>] [--field <name>=<value>]… [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig task show <task> [--findings] [--notes] [--history] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig task edit <task> [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0 saved, or nothing changed; 1 a field changed underneath the edit, nothing written; 2 on any error, including no terminal and no $VISUAL/$EDITOR, or a file that does not parse rig task list [--state <s>]… [--all] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig task move <task> <state> [--sha <sha>] [--pr <n>] [--reason <text>] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0 moved; 1 refused by a gate or the workflow, nothing written; 2 on any error rig task set <task> --field <name>=<value>… [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 1 a field changed underneath, nothing written; 2 on any error rig task count <task> <counter> [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig task is <task> <state> [--repo <dir>] 0 the effective state is <state>; 1 it is not; 2 on any error rig task log <task> [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig finding add <task> --severity <sev> --summary <text> [--path <p[:line]>] [--key <k>] [--field <name>=<value>]… [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0, also for a duplicate; 2 on any error rig finding list <task> [--status <s>]… [--blocking] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig finding set <task> <finding> --status <s> [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig note add [<task>] --kind <k> --text <text> [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig note list [<task>] [--kind <k>] [--limit <n>] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig workflow show [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig workflow validate [<file>] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0 valid; 1 invalid; 2 on any error rig next [--who agent\|human] [--limit <n>] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig context <task> [--budget <tokens>] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig config get <key> [--global\|--repo\|--local] [--json] 0; 1 not set; 2 error or unknown key rig config set <key> <value> --global\|--repo\|--local 0; 2 on any error rig config unset <key> --global\|--repo\|--local 0, also when not set; 2 on any error rig config list [--global\|--repo\|--local] [--show-origin] [--json] 0; 2 on any error rig login 0; 1 a login failed; 2 on any error rig login github\|gitlab\|jira [--url <site>] [--user <email>] [--repo] [--store keychain\|file] 0; 1 the login failed or Jira rejected the token, nothing stored; 2 on any error rig login status [--json] 0; 2 on any error rig logout jira [--url <site>] [--repo] 0, also when already logged out; 2 on any error, including a store that could not be checked when the entry was found nowhere rig logout github\|gitlab 2: prints the gh/glab command that does it

An unknown flag is always exit 2: rig never ignores an argument it does not understand. In the phase-2 commands, exit 1 means refused by a gate or the workflow with nothing written, and exit 2 covers usage errors, an unknown or ambiguous task, a bad workflow file, and store or git errors. The commands' flags and behaviour are described in phase-2.md and phase-2.5.md, and the workflow file in workflows.md. RIG_ACTOR names who acted and RIG_WORKFLOW the workflow to use; RIG_JIRA_TOKEN overrides a stored Jira token at use time.

Stable text output

  • rig pr wait, green: exactly one line, CI green: PR #<n> or CI green: run <id>. Red: CI red: … first, then the failed names, then at most 40 log lines after --- log tail ---. Errors go to stderr with the prefix ci-wait:.
  • rig pr list, and the pull request lines of rig status: #<n> <ci> <head> <title, at most 50 characters>, then conflict and draft when they apply.
  • rig push, on success: pushed <branch> to origin.

Stable JSON fields

A pull request, from rig pr view --json and each element of rig pr list --json:

Field Value number integer url, title, head, headSha, base strings state open, closed or merged draft boolean mergeable mergeable, conflicting or unknown mergeSha the merge commit; present only once merged ci red, running, green or none checks array of {name, state, url}; state is pass, fail, cancel, pending or skipped

rig pr checks --json is {number, ci, checks} with the same meanings.

rig status --json is {handoff, tasks, worktrees, prs, prsError}: handoff is {written, lines} or absent; tasks is an array of task file names without .md; each worktree is {path, branch, ahead, dirty}; prs holds pull requests as above; prsError is present when the forge could not be reached, and the rest of the output is still valid.

docs.title: What rig push does and does not guarantee
docs.text:
Any command line that starts rig push can only make a non-forced push of one local branch named <prefix>/<name> to the branch of the same name on origin. It cannot name main or any bare branch, a tag, a refspec, another remote, or a force or delete option. Exit 2 means git push never started.

Two things sit outside that guarantee.

  • .claude/rig.json is the user's file. Its pushPrefixes decide which prefixes count, so whoever can write it can widen the pushes: to release/x, say, though still never to a bare branch, a tag or a force. An agent must not edit it. The project settings template makes any Edit or Write of .claude/rig.json, in the project or in a worktree below it, and any shell command that names rig.json, ask first (tests/rig-settings.bats pins those rules). A permission rule matches text, so this is a barrier, not a proof: a shell command can build the file name without spelling it, and two commands the template already allows can write and run a file (git log --output=<path> and rg --pre <program>). Narrowing those allow rules is a separate change.
  • Git's own configuration is not constrained. A pre-push hook, or remote.origin.receivepack, runs whatever it says during any push, and an agent can set either with git config. rig push runs the repository's hooks like any push does, so it does not close this. The raw git push origin task/<name> form the push guard allows has the same limit. Closing it would mean pushing with hooks disabled, which would also disable the hooks a project relies on; that trade has not been made.

docs.title: The forge port
docs.text:
type Forge interface {
    ViewPR(ctx context.Context, ref string) (PullRequest, error)
    ListPRs(ctx context.Context, opts ListOptions) ([]PullRequest, error)
    CreatePR(ctx context.Context, in CreatePRInput) (PullRequest, error)
    Checks(ctx context.Context, pr int) ([]Check, error)
    WaitChecks(ctx context.Context, target WaitTarget) (WaitResult, error)
    FailedLogs(ctx context.Context, target WaitTarget, failed []Check) ([]LogLine, error)
}

type PullRequest struct {
    Number    int
    URL       string
    Title     string
    State     PRState   // open | closed | merged
    Draft     bool
    Head      string    // head branch
    HeadSHA   string
    Base      string
    Mergeable Mergeable // mergeable | conflicting | unknown
    Checks    []Check
}

type Check struct {
    Name  string
    State CheckState // pass | fail | cancel | pending | skipped
    URL   string
}

WaitTarget is a pull request number or a CI run id. Later phases add Merge, Comment and Reviews.

A pull request's overall CI state is derived from its checks in one place, in the port, so both adapters report it the same way: red if any check failed or was cancelled, else running if any is pending, else green if there is at least one check, else none.

docs.title: Phase 1 commands
docs.text:
Command What it does Exit codes rig push <task-id\|branch> [--worktree <path>] Pushes one loop branch to origin 0 pushed, 1 rejected by the remote, 2 refused rig pr view\|list\|checks Prints neutral output from the forge 0, 2 on error rig pr open --head <branch> … Opens a pull request. Never pushes, and takes its body only from --body, never from a file 0, 2 on error rig pr wait <pr> or --run <id> Blocks until CI finishes 0 green, 1 red, 2 error or timeout rig status [--json] The session brief, worktrees and one line per open PR 0

rig push is the security-relevant command. It resolves a task id to its branch (task/<id>-<slug>, the slug taken from docs/plan/tasks/<id>-*.md, the same lookup as derive_slug in scripts/_wt-common.sh). It then refuses, with exit 2 and without running git, anything that is not a plain branch name under a configured prefix: a refspec (a:b), a + prefix, a .. segment, a tag, any force or delete flag, and any unknown flag. What remains is run as git -C <worktree> push -u origin <branch>:<branch> — an argument vector, so there is nothing for a shell to reinterpret.

rig pr wait keeps the contract of scripts/ci-wait.sh, so callers do not change: the same exit codes, CI green: PR #N as the only line when green, the failed checks and a 40-line log tail when red, and CI_WAIT_TIMEOUT (seconds, default 1800). ci-wait.sh becomes a wrapper that execs rig pr wait.

rig status prints one line per open pull request in the format commands/status.md already uses: #N red|running|green|none branch title [conflict] [draft].

Phase 1 is read-only on documents. State still comes from the existing docs/plan files, git and the forge.

docs.title: The store and workflows (phase 2)
docs.text:
A store holds work in progress outside the code tree: one append-only event log per task under refs/rig/tasks/<ULID>, local to the clone unless the user opts in to sharing it. A task's state is a fold over its events. Which states exist, which transitions are allowed and which gates guard them come from a workflow file, not from rig. Tasks, findings and notes carry typed fields the workflow declares. phase-2.md has the format, the commands and the extension points.

The state machine this section used to define (planned → implementing → reviewed → verified@sha → pr_open → ci_green → ready → merged) is now claude-kit's workflow file, shown in phase-2.md as the worked example.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
Phase What it delivers 0 This document, and a baseline of permission prompts and tokens per task 1 rig push, rig pr, rig status, rig version; the github and gitlab adapters; the kit's commands and agents switched to them 1.5 cli/ moves to its own repository, AindriuB/rig, with its history; the kit installs a pinned release 2 Shipped in 0.3.0. Generic core: the store port and git-ref backend, workflow files with gates and hooks, rig task, rig finding, rig note, rig workflow, rig next, rig context. The kit's loop is a test fixture, not built in 2.5 Shipped in 0.3.0. rig config (global, per-repo and local scopes; forge and tracker settings) and rig login/rig logout with keychain-held tokens 3 Views and exports: Markdown and HTML renderings of tasks, notes and history from the store, by template, for any workflow. Importers for existing plans (the kit's docs/plan first) as programs the user runs 4 Team scale: opt-in rig sync of the store, rig claim, retention and rig gc, a search index rebuilt from refs, and tracker adapters (jira, github, gitlab, and exec for any program) 5 Metrics from event logs, for any workflow: time in each state, counter values, stop reasons, findings by path 6 An MCP server over the same core; each workflow transition becomes a typed tool 1.0 The kit-specific parts of phase 1 (.claude/rig.json, claude-handoff.md and docs/plan/tasks reads, default push prefixes) move behind config or are dropped, as a major change

README, architecture, conventions, release notes and ADRs stay in the tree throughout. Plans, tasks, findings and history are what move into the store, for the projects that choose to use it. The kit's own changes to become one consumer of these actions are a follow-up in the kit's repository.

docs.title: Version bump
docs.text:
• File: cmd/rig/version.go — set version to <version>.
  • Commit: release: <version> on a task/release-<version> branch; PR to main.
  • Wait: CI ci.yml green on the PR, then merge.
  • Skip when go run ./cmd/rig version on main already prints <version>.

docs.title: Tag
docs.text:
• git tag -a v<version> -m "<version>" on main's head, then git push origin v<version>.
  • release.yml refuses a tag that does not match rig version.

docs.title: Publish targets
docs.text: Target Triggered by Workflow Secret it needs GitHub release (draft, 5 binaries + SHA256SUMS) tag push release.yml none (GITHUB_TOKEN) GitHub release published gh release edit v<version> --draft=false --latest none (manual) none

docs.title: Verify the published state
docs.text:
• gh release view v<version> --json isDraft,assets --jq '.isDraft, [.assets[].name]' prints false and rig-{linux-amd64,linux-arm64,darwin-amd64,darwin-arm64,windows-amd64.exe}, SHA256SUMS.
  • go install github.com/AindriuB/rig/cmd/rig@v<version> in a temp GOBIN, then rig version prints <version>.

docs.title: If a step fails
docs.text: • Do not delete or move a pushed tag. Fix forward with <version+patch>.

docs.title: Writing a workflow
docs.text: A workflow tells rig what states a task moves through, which moves are allowed, and what must be true before each move. rig has no lifecycle of its own: the rules live in a JSON file you choose. This page is the reference for that file. phase-2.md explains why the store and workflows exist; this page explains how to write one.

docs.title: Choosing the workflow rig uses
docs.text:
rig loads one workflow per command, from the first of these that is set:

  1. RIG_WORKFLOW, a preset name or an absolute path to a file.
  2. The workflow config key (a preset name or an absolute path). It is read only from the global file, ~/.rig/config.json, and rig config set refuses it: you edit the file by hand.
  3. The built-in preset basic.

A relative path is refused. rig never looks for a workflow inside a repository, so cloning a repository never makes rig run its programs.

rig workflow show prints the workflow in effect and where it came from. rig workflow validate [<file>] checks a file, or the one in effect, and reports any task that is in a state the workflow does not have. It exits 0 when valid, 1 when invalid and 2 on an error.

docs.title: The basic preset
docs.text:
open -> active -> done        any -> stopped        stopped -> (the state before)

States are open (action start), active (action finish), done (final) and stopped (action decide, for a human). Moving to stopped needs a reason. There are no gates. Findings have two severities, blocking and info. Use rig workflow show --json to see the exact file.

docs.title: The file
docs.text:
A workflow is one JSON object. rig refuses a key it does not know, so a typo is an error and not a silent no-op.

Key Meaning name, version A label and a positive integer. A task records both when it is created. initial The state a new task starts in. branch Branch name template; {short}, {slug} and {id} are replaced. Optional. states An object: state name to {action, who, final, shaBound}, all optional. onNewCommit The state a sha-bound task counts as in when its branch has moved on. Needed if any state is sha-bound. transitions The allowed moves, in order (see below). fields Typed fields on tasks. findings {severities: [...], fields: {...}}. counters Names of counters a task can carry. hooks Programs to run after a move.

docs.title: States
docs.text:
• action is a label that rig next prints for a task in this state, such as review or merge. rig attaches no meaning to it.
  • who is agent (the default) or human. rig next --who human lists the tasks waiting on a person.
  • final: true means no transition leaves the state, and rig task list hides tasks in it unless you pass --all. A final state cannot be sha-bound.
  • shaBound: true ties a task to the commit it was moved in at. When the task's branch head is no longer that commit, the task's effective state is onNewCommit. This is worked out when the task is read; nothing is written. onNewCommit itself must be neither final nor sha-bound.

State names may not be empty, *, or start with $.

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
{ "from": ["a", "b"], "to": "c", "takes": "sha", "count": "rounds", "gates": [ ... ] }
  • from is a state, a list of states, or * for every non-final state other than the target. to is a state, or $previous.
  • $previous means the state the task was in before its latest move. A task that has never moved has none, and the move is refused. rig next shows such a move as blocked by previous.
  • takes names an argument the move records: sha (--sha), pr (--pr) or reason (--reason). A move that takes one refuses to run without it.
  • count adds one to the named counter when the move is written.
  • A move into a sha-bound state that takes no sha inherits the sha of the sha-bound state it came from, so verified -> pr_open carries verified's sha. Otherwise it records none and the state keeps the sha it was last entered at.
  • gates are checked in order before anything is written. Every gate is evaluated and the move happens only if all pass. A refusal is exit 1 and writes nothing. There is no --force: to get past a gate, change the file.

Routes must be unique. After from lists and * are expanded, no two transitions may take the same state to the same target, and one transition may not name a route twice. So {"from": "*", "to": "X"} beside {"from": "a", "to": "X"} is refused, because * already covers a. rig workflow validate reports each clash as route a -> X is also taken by transitions[N]. To give one state different rules from the rest, list the other states explicitly instead of using *.

Validation also requires that every transition names declared states, that no transition leaves a final state, and that every state can be reached from initial. Each problem is reported with its JSON path, for example transitions[3].gates[0].shaIsHead.

docs.title: Gates
docs.text:
A gate is an object with one key, the gate's name.

Gate Passes when {"noOpenFindings": {"severity": ["P1", "P2"]}} no finding with one of those severities is open. Each severity must be declared in findings.severities. {"shaIsHead": true} the sha the move was given is the branch head. The move must take sha. {"shaIs": "<state>"} the sha the move was given is the one recorded when the task entered <state>. The move must take sha. {"dependsIn": ["merged"]} every task named in the depends field is in one of those states. The workflow must declare a depends field of type tasks. A dependency in a sha-bound state is judged by its effective state. {"fieldSet": "<field>"} the field has a value. title and body count as fields. {"counterBelow": {"counter": "rounds", "max": 4}} the counter is below max. max is at least 1. {"command": ["program", "arg", "{short}"]} the program exits 0.

A command gate gets the task as JSON on standard input and has 30 seconds. rig next never runs one: it reports the move's ok as null and the gate as "ok": null, meaning "not run". Only rig task move runs them.

docs.title: Fields, severities and counters
docs.text:
Task fields have a type: string, text, int, bool, list, enum (with values), paths (file globs) or tasks (task references). title and body are built in and cannot be declared. Two flags change how a field is used:

  • context: true prints the field in the fixed part of rig context.
  • owns: true marks the one paths field rig context uses to find the task's files. At most one task field may carry it.

findings.fields are the extra fields a finding takes, such as a route enum. They cannot carry owns. A finding's severity must be one of findings.severities; NOTE or any severity no noOpenFindings gate names never blocks anything.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
{ "on": "enter:stopped", "run": ["notify-user", "{short}", "{reason}"] }

on is enter:<state>, leave:<state> or transition. Hooks run, in file order, after a move has been written. A hook gets {event, task} as JSON on standard input and has 30 seconds. A hook that fails is reported on standard error, and in hookErrors with --json, but it never undoes the move. Something that must be able to refuse a move is a command gate, not a hook.

docs.title: Arguments and placeholders
docs.text: command gates and hooks are argument vectors. rig runs the program directly and never through a shell. An argument that is exactly {short}, {id}, {slug}, {state}, {reason} or {sha} is replaced by that value, and the value stays one argument whatever it contains, spaces and ; included. A placeholder inside longer text, such as --to={state}, is refused by validation. In a hook {state} is the state entered; in a gate it is the state the move leaves.

docs.title: Worked example: the claude-kit loop
docs.text:
claude-kit's plan, implement, review, verify, pull request, merge loop is one workflow among others. The file below is the fixture rig tests against (internal/workflow/testdata/claude-kit-loop.json); the kit owns its real copy.

{
  "name": "claude-kit-loop",
  "version": 1,
  "initial": "planned",
  "branch": "task/{short}-{slug}",
  "states": {
    "planned":      { "action": "implement" },
    "implementing": { "action": "review" },
    "reviewed":     { "action": "verify" },
    "verified":     { "action": "open-pr",  "shaBound": true },
    "pr_open":      { "action": "wait-ci",  "shaBound": true },
    "ci_green":     { "action": "mark-ready", "shaBound": true },
    "ready":        { "action": "merge", "who": "human", "shaBound": true },
    "merged":       { "final": true },
    "stopped":      { "action": "decide", "who": "human" }
  },
  "onNewCommit": "implementing",
  "transitions": [
    { "from": "planned", "to": "implementing",
      "gates": [{ "dependsIn": ["merged"] }] },
    { "from": "implementing", "to": "reviewed",
      "gates": [{ "noOpenFindings": { "severity": ["P1", "P2", "STYLE", "SPEC"] } }] },
    { "from": "reviewed", "to": "verified", "takes": "sha",
      "gates": [{ "shaIsHead": true }] },
    { "from": "reviewed", "to": "implementing", "count": "rounds",
      "gates": [{ "counterBelow": { "counter": "rounds", "max": 4 } }] },
    { "from": "verified", "to": "pr_open", "takes": "pr" },
    { "from": "pr_open", "to": "ci_green", "takes": "sha",
      "gates": [{ "shaIs": "verified" }] },
    { "from": "ci_green", "to": "ready" },
    { "from": "ready", "to": "merged", "takes": "sha" },
    { "from": ["verified", "pr_open", "ci_green", "ready"], "to": "implementing" },
    { "from": "*", "to": "stopped", "takes": "reason" },
    { "from": "stopped", "to": "$previous" }
  ],
  "fields": {
    "acceptance": { "type": "list", "context": true },
    "owns":       { "type": "paths", "context": true, "owns": true },
    "depends":    { "type": "tasks" }
  },
  "findings": {
    "severities": ["P1", "P2", "P3", "STYLE", "SPEC", "NOTE"],
    "fields": { "route": { "type": "enum", "values": ["implementer", "orchestrator"] } }
  },
  "counters": ["rounds"],
  "hooks": [
    { "on": "enter:stopped", "run": ["notify-user", "{short}", "{reason}"] }
  ]
}

Reading it through:

  • Starting. A task begins in planned. It cannot move to implementing until every task in its depends field is merged.
  • Review. implementing -> reviewed is refused while any P1, P2, STYLE or SPEC finding is open. P3 and NOTE findings never block.
  • Verifying. reviewed -> verified takes the sha that was reviewed and needs it to be the branch head. verified, pr_open, ci_green and ready are sha-bound, so a new commit on the branch drops the task back to implementing with no one having to notice. rig task is <t> verified answers "was this verified at the current head?" with one exit code.
  • Rounds. reviewed -> implementing is the only way back from reviewed. It counts a round and is refused once rounds reaches 4. The from-list of the plain -> implementing transition therefore leaves reviewed out: if it were there, the same route would exist twice, and validation would refuse the file, and the round cap could be skipped.
  • Pull request. verified -> pr_open records the pull request number and carries verified's sha. pr_open -> ci_green needs the sha it is given to be the one recorded at verified.
  • Merge. ready is for a human. ready -> merged is final.
  • Stopping. From any state but merged, a task can be stopped with a reason, which runs the notify-user hook. stopped -> $previous returns it to the state it left.

docs.title: When the workflow changes under a task
docs.text: A task records the workflow's name and version when it is created, but gates use the workflow loaded now. A task in a state the current workflow lacks is reported by rig workflow validate, and by rig next with the action unknown-state. A * transition can still move it.
